newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks end lower, led down by Bavaria.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks end lower, led down by Bavaria.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended lower in thin trading that saw profit-taking knock some of the suds out of brewer Bavaria SA.

Medellin IBOMED general price index slipped a barely noticeable 0.05 percent to end at 13,513.97 on a lower-than- average volume of just 793.8 million pesos. Bogota's IBB fell 0.48 percent, however, closing at 863.08 on a lackluster volume of 821 million pesos.
"The market continues to be hit by widespread apathy," one broker said in a telephone interview.
"There are sporadic investments by foreign funds and speculative moves in leading stocks, but you can't see any firm trend," he added.

The day's biggest mover by far in Bogota was actively traded Bavaria, which fell 9.74 percent to end at 3,800 pesos per share. Brokers said the stock had moved sharply higher in recent weeks on the back of the purchase of about 2,500 shares by a foreign fund and local investors decided it was time to reap in the windfall profits.
Supermarket chain Carulla also fell on profit-taking, dropping 9.47 percent to end the day at 5,400 pesos a share.

Among the day's few gainers was Banco Ganadero, whose ordinary shares rose 1.08 in Medellin to close at 280 pesos per share. Banco de Bogota also firmed in Medellin, ending up 0.42 percent at 5,900 pesos per share.
